title: Before First Light
logline: A night-shift watchman fights sleep through the small hours, and when his attention finally sinks, his body slumps with it, and has to be caught and held up again.
human_question: What keeps a body upright, when the mind that is supposed to hold it up can barely stay awake?

premise.story: One long night shift, from the quiet after midnight to the change in the body and the light at dawn, told through a watchman's own routines and reasons for the work.
premise.place: A tea or rubber estate factory, or a security post, kept awake through the night by one or two people.
premise.experience: The stretched, echoing quiet of the small hours, a head dropping and snapping back, tea made to stay awake, and the visible change in the body when the sky lightens.

concept_links.why: The source uses exactly this situation: mind-born matter is what moves the body and holds its posture, arising only at the instant of a thought. When the mind sinks into its faint sleep-state, the body can no longer hold itself up, and a sitting or standing person who dozes off falls.
Lightness and workability of the body are described as coming and going with sleep, food, weather and mood; a long night shift is where their absence is most visible.

what_camera_could_observe: Posture slowly collapsing in a chair through the small hours
The head dropping and snapping back, a hand gripping a torch or rail
A tea break or a walk taken specifically to stay upright
Ordinary rounds and checks repeated through the night
The visible change in the body when dawn comes and the shift ends
what_must_be_real: The worker's actual shift, routines and reasons for the job. Nothing staged; fatigue must never be framed as a personal failing rather than a real labour condition, and the worker must not be exposed to disciplinary risk by the filming.

possible_arc.opening: The quiet that settles in after midnight.
possible_arc.turn: The fight between attention and gravity, hour by hour.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the body and the worker actually do when the shift ends.

position_hint: opening candidate: a body shaped by the hours it keeps, at the very edge of what the mind can hold up, and a possible point for Object 7 to be acquired if a real moment allows it

requirements: A genuine night shift with a worker willing to be filmed over several nights
Employer permission that does not put the worker's job at risk
Enough low light to film without disturbing the work

suggestions.name: A tea or rubber estate factory running a night shift
suggestions.region: Central Highlands (e.g. Hatton/Dikoya or Nuwara Eliya district)
suggestions.why: Estate factories are well documented as running through the night during processing season.
suggestions.season_notes: Depends on the estate's processing calendar.
suggestions.verify: A specific estate, its night-shift practice and management permission are unverified.

risks: Could mock or expose a worker who might be disciplined for dozing on duty
Framing fatigue as a personal failing rather than a labour condition
drop_if: No willing worker and employer consent that protects the worker's job
Filming would itself put the worker at risk of discipline

connections.note: Both watch attention keep a tired body going through a long stretch of work, one through the night, one through a harvest day.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
